summary: Sun and Moon in one sign (a new-Moon birth) is read classically as practical, technical skill (machinery, stone, metal work) and cleverness in work, with a tendency to be guided by one's spouse. The Moon is weak here because it is close to the Sun.
common_outcomes: skill with machines, stone or metal work
clever and capable in whatever work is taken up
strongly guided by or devoted to the spouse
rare_outcomes: immodest or able to deceive (Saravali; the translator gives 'metallurgist' with 'able to deceive' as an alternative reading)

by_area.personality: Clever and capable in work (Jataka Parijata 8.1); Saravali 15.2 adds a less modest, possibly calculating side.
by_area.career: Machinery and stone work (Brihat Jataka 14.1; Phaladeepika 18.1); metal work or trade in intoxicants (Saravali 15.2).
by_area.finance: Saravali 15.2 says quite wealthy; V. Subrahmanya Sastri's note on Brihat Jataka 14 treats the new-Moon conjunction as the one Sun conjunction that is not bad for money.
by_area.relationships: Under the influence of the wife or of women (Saravali 15.2); submissive to the wife (Jataka Parijata 8.1).

strengtheners: Saravali 15.23: results increase when both planets occupy good vargas (divisions).
weakeners_or_cancellations: The Moon is combust (astangata) within 12 degrees of the Sun (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII); Frawley gives a 15-degree orb for the Moon.
Frawley: the Moon is weakest as it approaches the Sun and strongest when full.
Saravali 5.27: a combust planet loses its power to give good results and can give bad results in full.
Saravali 15.23: results decrease when the planets occupy bad vargas.
lagna_or_context_notes: The classical two-planet results are general and apply in any house; Jataka Parijata (note to Adhyaya 8) says house-by-house results for each pair are given in other works (Horaratna), which were not read here.

named_yogas.name: Amavasya (new-Moon) birth
named_yogas.source: V. Subrahmanya Sastri, note on Brihat Jataka 14.1

source_views.view: One who makes things of stone and builds machines.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.1 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, 2nd ed.)
source_views.view: Skilled in machinery and stone work; the note calls it a creative combination and the one Sun conjunction that is not bad for finance (the new-Moon conjunction).
Skilled in machinery and stone work (same as Brihat Jataka).

source_views.source: Saravali 15.2 (English tr., archive.org 'Kalyana Varmas Saravali'; translator not named)
source_views.view: Under the control of his wife or women, immodest, a metal worker (or deceptive), quite wealthy, expert in selling intoxicants.
Submissive to his wife and clever in every task.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII (Eighth House, Astangata Harana)
source_views.view: The Moon within 12 degrees of the Sun is astangata (combust).

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, Planetary Aspects and Combinations (pp. 175-176)
source_views.view: The Moon's combustion orb is 15 degrees; it weakens as it nears the Sun; planetary-war rules do not apply to the Sun or Moon.

disagreements: Brihat Jataka and Phaladeepika stress technical skill; Saravali adds immodesty, wealth and trade in intoxicants; Jataka Parijata stresses being clever and submissive to the wife. On combustion, Raman gives 12 degrees for the Moon and Frawley 15.
phrasing_guidance: Present it as a practical, hands-on, capable nature and a close bond with the partner. Mention that the Moon is faint near the Sun as a reason feelings may be kept inside, not as a defect. Leave out the intoxicants and deception readings unless strongly supported elsewhere.

summary: Sun with Mars gives strength, energy and a fiery, forceful temperament; the classical texts warn that the same force can turn harsh, untruthful or destructive.
common_outcomes: risk of harsh or unscrupulous conduct

by_area.personality: Splendid, brave, strong and fierce but quick to lie and harsh (Saravali 15.3); illustrious and energetic but untruthful (Jataka Parijata 8.1); fiery (Frawley).
by_area.health: Frawley: Mars with the Sun often makes the constitution fiery.

strengtheners: Saravali 15.23: results improve when both occupy good vargas.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mars is combust within 17 degrees of the Sun (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII); Frawley gives 8 degrees 30 minutes.
Saravali 5.27: a combust planet loses its power for good.
Frawley: a planet in a favourable sign or house can largely offset combustion.

source_views.view: One who takes pleasure in wrongdoing.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.1 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Intent on sinful deeds; the note calls it a destructive combination.
Inclined to sinful deeds.
Splendid, brave, strong but slow-witted; untruthful, sinful, inclined to harm and fierce.
Illustrious, strong and energetic, but untruthful and wicked.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, Medical Astrology (p. 217)
source_views.view: Mars conjunct the Sun often makes a person fiery.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII
source_views.view: Mars is combust within 17 degrees of the Sun.

disagreements: All texts read agree on strength and harshness; Saravali and Jataka Parijata add splendour and fame, Brihat Jataka gives only the negative. Combustion orb: Raman 17 degrees, Frawley 8.5 degrees.
phrasing_guidance: Describe drive, courage and a strong will, and suggest directing it into constructive challenges. Do not call the person sinful or violent; frame the classical warning as a need to watch temper and bluntness.

summary: Sun with Mercury forms Budha-Aditya yoga: intelligence, skill, learning and a good name. Most authorities rate it well; its strength depends on Mercury not being too deeply combust.
common_outcomes: clever, intelligent and skilful in work

by_area.personality: Clever, intelligent, sweet-spoken, noble (Brihat Jataka 14.1; Saravali 15.4); learned but somewhat fickle (Jataka Parijata 8.1).
by_area.career: In service, dear to the king and good people (Saravali 15.4); skilful in all work (Raman, PVR).
by_area.finance: Fame and money but unsteady wealth (Saravali 15.4); Sastri's note says it is not good for finance.

strengtheners: Raman (Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 24): Mercury should be more than 10 degrees from the Sun for the yoga to work.
PVR Narasimha Rao: strongest in divisional charts such as the D-10; works in the rasi chart when Mercury is not combust.
Raman (How to Judge a Horoscope, chart 202): Jupiter's aspect on a combust Mercury largely removes the harm of combustion.
Saravali 15.23: good vargas increase the results.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Mercury is combust within 14 degrees of the Sun, 12 when retrograde (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII); Frawley gives 2 degrees.
Raman (How to Judge a Horoscope, chart 202): combust Mercury is said to make one superficial and short of judgement.
PVR: yogas formed by combust planets lose some of their power to do good.
lagna_or_context_notes: PVR: the yoga gives its results in the periods of the Sun and Mercury (and of the sign holding them).

named_yogas.name: Budha-Aditya yoga (Nipuna yoga)
named_yogas.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 24; PVR Narasimha Rao 11.2.4

source_views.view: Clever and intelligent, gains reputation and comfort (Neely's rendering adds a harsh streak).

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.1 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Clever, intelligent, famous and happy; the note says it gives proficiency and a good name but is not good for finance.
Clever, intelligent, famous and happy.
In service, unsteady wealth, sweet speech, fame and money, noble, liked by the king and good people, with strength, beauty and learning.
Learning, beauty and strength, but fickle-minded.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 24 Budha-Aditya Yoga
source_views.view: Highly intelligent, skilful, well regarded and comfortable; Mercury is usually an exception to the harm of combustion but should be more than 10 degrees from the Sun; not rare.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XIV (chart 202)
source_views.view: Almost all standard works call the Sun-Mercury combination auspicious; combust Mercury can make one superficial, but Jupiter's aspect largely cancels this.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 11.2.4
source_views.view: Intelligent, skilful, well known, respected and happy; combustion reduces it; most powerful in the D-10.

disagreements: Saravali and Sastri's note say wealth is unsteady or weak while Raman and PVR give comfort and happiness. Combustion orb for Mercury: Raman 14 degrees (12 retrograde) in How to Judge a Horoscope, 10 degrees for the yoga in Three Hundred Important Combinations; Frawley 2 degrees.
phrasing_guidance: Present as a sharp, capable, articulate mind and a good reputation. If Mercury is very close to the Sun, say the gift may need focus and patience to show fully rather than calling it cancelled.

summary: Sun with Jupiter is read as a person devoted to work for others, often in an advisory, ministerial or teaching role; texts disagree on whether the nature is kind or stern.
rare_outcomes: a stern or cruel streak (Sastri's translation of Brihat Jataka and Phaladeepika)
minister of a king or preceptor (Saravali)

by_area.personality: Virtuous, good-minded (Saravali 15.5); full of faith and active (Jataka Parijata 8.1); Sastri's Brihat Jataka and Phaladeepika also call him cruel.
by_area.career: Minister or preceptor (Saravali 15.5); pleases the king through his work (Jataka Parijata 8.1); devoted to other people's work (Brihat Jataka 14.1).
by_area.finance: Wealthy (Jataka Parijata 8.1); gains through friends (Saravali 15.5).

strengtheners: Saravali 15.23: good vargas increase the results.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Jupiter is combust within 11 degrees of the Sun (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII); Frawley gives 8 degrees 30 minutes.
Saravali 5.27: a combust planet loses its power for good.

source_views.view: Devotes himself to the work of others.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.1 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Cruel and engaged in other people's work; the note says cruel-hearted and benefits others at his own cost.
Cruel, yet interested in helping others.
Virtuous, a king's minister, gains through friends, good-minded, a preceptor.
Full of faith, active, pleases the king through his work, wealthy.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII
source_views.view: Jupiter is combust within 11 degrees of the Sun.

disagreements: The 'cruel' reading appears in Sastri's translations of Brihat Jataka and Phaladeepika but not in Neely's Brihat Jataka, Saravali or Jataka Parijata, which are positive (virtue, faith, ministerial role). Combustion orb: Raman 11 degrees, Frawley 8.5.
phrasing_guidance: Lead with service, guidance and principled work for others. Do not call the person cruel; at most mention a firm, strict side.

summary: Sun with Venus is linked classically to earning through performance or arms, public entertainment, and money or connections through women or the spouse; Venus is weakened by combustion.
common_outcomes: earns through performing, acting or entertaining the public
gains or ties through women or the spouse's family

by_area.personality: Mighty and able to amuse people (Saravali 15.6); intelligent (Jataka Parijata 8.2); Sastri's note calls it an imitative spirit.
by_area.career: Earns as an actor or through weapons (Brihat Jataka 14.1; Phaladeepika 18.1); skilled with weapons and entertains the public (Saravali 15.6).
by_area.finance: Much money earned through women (Saravali 15.6).
by_area.family: Respects and attends to the relatives gained through his wife (Jataka Parijata 8.2).

strengtheners: Saravali 15.23: good vargas increase the results.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Venus is combust within 10 degrees of the Sun, 8 when retrograde (Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII); Frawley gives 4 degrees.
Frawley: Venus, like Mercury and the Moon, is weaker the closer it is to the Sun.
lagna_or_context_notes: Raman notes that Venus is exempt from the combustion reduction in the longevity (ayurdaya) calculation; this is specific to that calculation.

source_views.view: Profits through weapons and warfare.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.1 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Earns as an actor or by weapons; note: an imitative spirit.
Earns as an actor or through weapons.
Skilled with weapons, mighty, weak-sighted in old age, entertains the public, much money through women.
Intelligent and attentive to the relatives acquired through his wife.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 2, ch. XII
source_views.view: Venus combust within 10 degrees (8 retrograde).

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, Planetary Aspects and Combinations (p. 175)
source_views.view: Venus combust within 4 degrees; inner planets are weaker near the Sun.

disagreements: Brihat Jataka, Phaladeepika and Saravali stress performance and weapons; Jataka Parijata gives only intelligence and attention to in-laws. Combustion orb: Raman 10 degrees, Frawley 4.
phrasing_guidance: Frame as charisma, a flair for performance or public life, and strong ties through the partner. Mention eyesight only as a general care point, never as a prediction.

summary: Sun with Saturn joins two enemies: classically it gives hard work and skill with metals or crafts, dutifulness, but strain with family or superiors and a sense of being held back.
common_outcomes: skilled in metal work or crafts
difficulties with superiors, opponents or the father
rare_outcomes: loss or separation concerning spouse and children (Saravali)
under the power of enemies (Jataka Parijata)

by_area.personality: Virtuous, mindful of duty, pure but not wholly straightforward (Saravali 15.7); somewhat slow-witted (Jataka Parijata 8.2); hardworking (Sastri's note).
by_area.career: Metal work or vessel-making (Brihat Jataka 14.1; Phaladeepika 18.1; Saravali 15.7).
by_area.finance: Sastri's note on Brihat Jataka 14 groups Sun conjunctions as bad for finance.
by_area.health: Raman: Sun in the 6th afflicted by Saturn points to heart trouble or chest pain unless Jupiter aspects.
by_area.relationships: Saravali 15.7 speaks of losing wife and son.
by_area.family: Rath: Saturn joining the Sun in the 6th shows enmity with the father.

strengtheners: Rath (Crux 9.2): if the Sun has a higher longitude than Saturn, the trouble is overcome.
Raman (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IX): Jupiter's aspect relieves the Sun-Saturn affliction in the 6th.
Saravali 15.23: good vargas increase the results.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Rath (Crux 9.2): if the Sun has a lower longitude than Saturn, the evil is more evident.

Saturn becomes combust near the Sun (Raman lists Saturn with the other planets; the scan reads 5 degrees, unverified); Frawley gives 8 degrees 30 minutes. Raman notes Saturn is exempt from the combustion reduction in the longevity calculation.
lagna_or_context_notes: House-specific notes read: in the 6th house (Raman; Rath).

source_views.view: Skilled in metal work, makes various kinds of vessels.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.1 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Clever in metal work; note: one who works hard.
Skilled in metal work or pottery.
Metal worker, virtuous and dutiful, loses wife and son, true to his family's ways, pure but not fully upright.
Somewhat dull-witted and in the power of his enemies.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IX (Sixth House)
source_views.view: Sun in the 6th afflicted by Saturn shows heart trouble or chest pain unless Jupiter aspects.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology 9.2 (in the same archive.org item)
source_views.view: Saturn conjoining the Sun in the 6th shows enmity with the father; the Sun at a higher longitude overcomes it, a lower longitude makes it worse.

disagreements: Saravali gives virtue and duty with family loss; Jataka Parijata gives dullness and enemies; Brihat Jataka and Phaladeepika give only craft. The Saturn combustion orb in Raman's scan (5 degrees) differs from Frawley's 8.5 degrees.
phrasing_guidance: Frame as discipline, endurance and achievement through steady effort, with lessons around authority and the father. Never predict loss of spouse or children; mention heart care only as general wellbeing.

summary: Sun with Rahu is an 'eclipse' combination in modern readings: the Sun's significations (self, father, vitality) are obstructed or transformed, and the result can lean either to worldly trouble or to spiritual renunciation. The classical two-planet chapters read do not cover the nodes.
common_outcomes: Sun's matters (self-confidence, father, authority) obstructed or unusual
possible pull towards spirituality or renunciation
rare_outcomes: Rath: this eclipse combination can produce either a saint or a criminal type, depending on other factors

by_area.personality: Rath: Rahu brings spirituality or renunciation while the Sun may turn negative; with lagna or arudha lagna in Aquarius the native is spiritual, in Leo the reverse.
by_area.health: Rath (Crux 9.2): Rahu eclipsing the Sun in the 6th shows torment by disease.
by_area.spirituality: Rath: Rahu with the Sun can show great spirituality or renunciation.

strengtheners: Rath (Crux 9.2): if the Sun has a higher longitude than Rahu, the evil is overcome.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Rath (Crux 9.2): if the Sun has a lower longitude than Rahu, the evil is more evident.
Frawley: closer conjunctions are stronger; a node conjoined with a planet acts as an eclipse of that planet.
lagna_or_context_notes: Rath: results depend on whether lagna or arudha lagna is Aquarius (spiritual) or Leo (worldly or negative).

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology 15.16 (chart 155) and 9.2
source_views.view: A close Sun-Rahu conjunction is an eclipse; Rahu shows great spirituality or renunciation while the Sun can be negative; in the 6th it shows disease, overcome when the Sun has the higher longitude.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology 12.13
source_views.view: An eclipse combination of the Sun can produce either a short-lived saint (Sun) or a long-lived criminal (Rahu).

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, The Planets (pp. 102-103)
source_views.view: A planet conjoined with either node is eclipsed: its energy is obstructed, negated or released; the nodes take on and magnify the planets they join.

disagreements: Brihat Jataka 14, Saravali 15, Jataka Parijata 8 and Phaladeepika 18 cover only the seven visible planets and say nothing on this pair. Rath's spiritual-versus-negative split is not found in Frawley, who stresses obstruction.
phrasing_guidance: Describe it as an intense, unusual relationship with authority, ego and the father, with a strong pull towards meaning or ambition. Avoid 'curse' or 'dosha' language; never predict illness.

summary: Sun with Ketu is treated in modern sources as an eclipse of the Sun: the Sun's significations are obstructed or turned inward. Frawley adds that Ketu can boost a planet that is strong in its own or exaltation sign. The classical two-planet chapters read do not cover the nodes.
common_outcomes: Sun's matters (self-confidence, father, status) obstructed or unusual
rare_outcomes: with a strong Sun, Ketu may boost its power (Frawley's general rule for Ketu)
strengtheners: Frawley: a planet in its own sign or exalted gains considerable power when conjoined with Ketu.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Frawley: conjunction with a node eclipses the planet, obstructing or negating its energy.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, The Planets (pp. 103, 105)
source_views.view: Node conjunctions eclipse a planet; Ketu boosts strong planets it joins (own sign or exalted); its results are sudden and unexpected, for good or ill.

disagreements: No classical two-planet chapter read covers this pair; only one modern source speaks to it.
phrasing_guidance: Keep it gentle: a reflective, less ego-driven expression of the self that may grow into inner strength. Do not predict harm to the father or health.

summary: Moon with Mars forms Chandra-Mangala yoga: a brave, energetic, emotionally intense nature and drive to earn. Classical texts warn of rough trades and friction with the mother; Raman and PVR stress material success.
common_outcomes: friction with the mother or women
rare_outcomes: trade in liquor, tools or women (Brihat Jataka; Phaladeepika)

by_area.personality: Valorous and brave (Saravali 15.8; Jataka Parijata 8.2); Raman: emotional, high-strung and hard to control in mind when Mars closely contacts the Moon.
by_area.career: Rough trades such as tools, liquor and earthenware (Brihat Jataka 14.2); artisan, metal or leather work (Saravali 15.8); Raman: earning through trades that cater to baser needs when afflicted, approved means when well placed.
by_area.finance: Raman: a powerful factor for stabilising finances; rich (Jataka Parijata 8.2); PVR: materially successful, possibly by unscrupulous means.
by_area.family: Disobedient to or harsh with the mother (Brihat Jataka 14.2 in Sastri's tr.; Phaladeepika 18.2; PVR; Raman citing the ancients).

strengtheners: Raman: most productive of good in the 2nd, 9th, 10th or 11th house.
Raman: when the Moon and Mars are well disposed, earnings come through approved means.
Saravali 5.40: a planet joined with the Moon is able to give happiness.
Saravali 15.23: good vargas increase the results.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Raman (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IX): Moon in the 6th afflicted by Mars and Saturn gives obscure, hard-to-cure illness and revengeful enemies.
lagna_or_context_notes: Raman holds the yoga also forms by mutual aspect (e.g. Moon in Taurus with Mars in Scorpio, Moon in Cancer with Mars in Capricorn) and calls those excellent; the conjunction-only definition is PVR's and the classical one.

named_yogas.name: Chandra-Mangala yoga (Sasi-Mangala)
named_yogas.source: Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations no. 6; PVR Narasimha Rao 11.3.5

source_views.view: Trades in liquor and is involved in schemes with deceitful women; an inauspicious combination.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.2 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Dealer in rough tools, women, drinks and earthen jars, disobedient to his mother; note: Varahamihira differs here from Parashara, who holds the yoga good.
Deals in tools, women, liquor or earthen jars; disobedient to his mother.
Valorous, brave in war, a boxer, prone to blood disorders, makes things of clay, skin and minerals; an artisan and metal worker.
Brave, of high birth, virtuous, rich and worthy.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Three Hundred Important Combinations, no. 6 Chandra Mangala Yoga
source_views.view: Gives the ancient results (unscrupulous earnings, harshness to mother), then argues the yoga strongly stabilises finances; good in the 2nd, 9th, 10th, 11th; also forms by mutual aspect.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IX (Sixth House)
source_views.view: Mars in close contact with the Moon shows a high-strung, emotional, erratic temperament with little control over the mind.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, 11.3.5
source_views.view: Worldly wise and materially successful; may earn by unscrupulous means; may treat mother or women badly.

disagreements: Varahamihira (and Phaladeepika) read it negatively; Jataka Parijata and, per Sastri's note, Parashara read it as good; Raman sides with the good reading for finance. Raman counts mutual aspect as forming the yoga; PVR and the classical texts require the same sign.
phrasing_guidance: Lead with drive, courage and earning ability, and note that strong feelings need a healthy outlet. Mention the mother relationship as an area for patience, not as conflict foretold; omit trades in women or liquor.

summary: Moon with Mercury, two benefics, gives pleasant, skilful speech, literary or interpretive talent, good fortune and reputation, and a charming manner.
common_outcomes: skill in interpreting, poetry or stories
rare_outcomes: devotion to the sciences and piety (Jataka Parijata)

by_area.personality: Courteous, resourceful, smiling and attractive (Brihat Jataka 14.2; Saravali 15.9); pious with varied merits (Jataka Parijata 8.2).
by_area.career: Clever at interpreting (Brihat Jataka 14.2 in Sastri's tr.); skilled in poetry and stories (Saravali 15.9).
by_area.finance: Wealthy (Saravali 15.9); Sastri's note says even this benefic pair is not good for finance.

strengtheners: Saravali 5.40: a planet joined with the Moon can give happiness.
Saravali 15.23: good vargas increase the results.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saravali 15.23: bad vargas reduce the results.
Raman (How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IX): a harmonious Moon-Mercury relationship is a great asset to the mind; affliction of either harms it.

source_views.view: Courteous speech, resourceful in reaching goals, reputation and good luck.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.2 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Sweet-tongued, clever in interpreting, lucky and famous; note: two benefics give good results, though not for finance.
Sweet speech, skilled at interpreting, good luck and fame.
Skilled in poems and stories, wealthy, kind to his wife, handsome, smiling, with distinct virtues.
Pious, devoted to the sciences, with many merits.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope vol. 1, ch. IX (Sixth House)
source_views.view: The Moon and Mercury are the two determinants of mental qualities; harmony between them is a great asset.

disagreements: Saravali calls the native wealthy; Sastri's note on Brihat Jataka says the pair is not good for finance.
phrasing_guidance: Present as a warm, witty communicator with a feel for words and stories. Keep wealth claims modest.

summary: Moon with Jupiter is one of the best two-planet combinations classically: intelligence, loyalty, respect for elders and the wise, family leadership and wealth, with Brihat Jataka adding a restless mind.
common_outcomes: head or protector of the family or a group
virtuous, respectful of the wise and the divine
intelligent and protective of good people
rare_outcomes: fickle or restless mind (Brihat Jataka; Phaladeepika)

by_area.personality: Bold but restless (Brihat Jataka 14.2); firm in friendship and modest (Saravali 15.10); very intelligent (Jataka Parijata 8.3).
by_area.career: Leader of a group (Brihat Jataka 14.2).
by_area.finance: Wealthy (Brihat Jataka 14.2; Saravali 15.10); Sastri's note calls it an exception to conjunctions being bad for finance, and elsewhere says it gives good wealth and constitution.
by_area.health: Good constitution (Sastri's note to Brihat Jataka ch. 18).
by_area.family: Chief of the family (Brihat Jataka 14.2 in Sastri's tr.); respectful to relatives (Saravali 15.10).
by_area.spirituality: Regards the gods and the wise (Saravali 15.10); protects good people (Jataka Parijata 8.3).

strengtheners: Saravali 5.40: a planet joined with the Moon can give happiness.
Saravali 15.23: good vargas increase the results.
weakeners_or_cancellations: Saravali 15.23: bad vargas reduce the results.

source_views.view: Bold, leads a group, restless mind, holds wealth.

source_views.source: Brihat Jataka 14.2 with notes (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri)
source_views.view: Overpowers enemies, fickle, head of the family, wealthy; note: an exception, good for finance.
Overpowers enemies but fickle; family chief and wealthy.
Firm in friendship, modest, respectful to relatives, wealthy, virtuous, honours gods and the learned.
Very intelligent and a protector of good people.

disagreements: Brihat Jataka and Phaladeepika add a restless or fickle mind; Saravali and Jataka Parijata do not.
phrasing_guidance: Speak of generosity, wisdom and a protective, family-minded nature, with a lively mind that benefits from routine.
